Posted September 6, 2002
Analysis By Richard Cowan

President Eisenhower's farewell address is widely remembered for his warning against the military-industrial complex. Such a warning is still worth hearing, but today one might do better to warn the people against the media-police state complex, a very unholy alliance between the media conglomerates and the police state propaganda machine.
See
Saving the Law from Law Enforcement. Ending the Police State Fraud. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
Author of Ottawa Citizen Series on Prohibition Blames The Media for the Drug War. Great Journalism Is The Antidote.
and for an overview of the subject of the role of the media and cannabis prohibition
see
Marijuana Prohibition, Media Criticism, Copyrights and the 8th and 9th Commandments.

A DEA spokesnark says, There is no medical marijuana That's a myth put out by people who want to legalize marijuana. We make no distinctions because there are none -- people who grow marijuana are marijuana traffickers. Our job is to enforce federal laws, and we surely will. "

The purpose of such an outrageous lie is not to convince anyone, especially in a county that voted overwhelmingly for medical cannabis, but rather to engender a sense of powerlessness in those who hear it.

In Nevada, Arizona, Ohio, and Michigan, where there are initiatives to lessen the power of the narks, the police and other government agencies violate the law by using Federal and local taxpayer money to oppose any change in the state laws.
See
The Governor's Sub-rosa Plot to Subvert an Election in Ohio By Dan Forbes

In the UK, the proposed change in the classification of cannabis to make possession a non-arrestable offense, which could be done administratively, is delayed until the basic law can be changed so the police can still arrest people for simple possession -- if they think there are aggravating circumstances.

The interim rules under which the police will operate until Parliament acts next year are being written by the police themselves.

A deputy assistant commissioner of the Metropolitan police, chairman of the Association of Chief Police Officers' drugs committee, is currently drawing up guidelines for officers to explain when the " aggravating factors " apply.

In any case, the exemption from arrest will apply only to less than three grams. In other words, the white upper middle class will have decrim, but non-whites and the lower class will still be arrested. The Canadian Government favors a similar approach.
See
Canadian Justice Minister Cites UK Move In Trial Balloon on " Decriminalization. " Police Want to Keep " Hammer. " Reporting from Haarlem in The Netherlands.

This will reduce the political pressure for meaningful change and increase the arbitrary power of the police when dealing with the cannon fodder classes.

From the prohibitionist perspective, the most dangerous aspect of the Canadian Senate Committee report is not the recommendation that cannabis be legalized. They will have no trouble stopping that, unless the Canadian Supreme Court does the job. (The Court will hear the arguments on December 13th and rule sometime next year.) The real threat to the prohibitionist enterprise in Canada and even in DEAland -- is the Committee's call for a national debate on cannabis prohibition.

This has a chance of working in Canada for two reasons.

First, many of the most influential newspapers are anti-prohibitionist and are calling for a national debate. The police, in their panic over possible changes in the laws have made the mistake of issuing their own call for a debate on a national drug strategy. That just means raising the penalties for growing cannabis.
See
The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan

The politicization of the Canadian police is largely the result of DEAland influence on pathetic Canadian SWAT-Team wannabees who have a bad case of muzzle-envy. Amusingly, David Griffin, the Canadian Police Association Executive Officer quoted Joe Califano twice in his televised response to the Canadian Senate report.
See
Califano Says, " Teens who smoke marijuana are playing a dangerous game of Russian roulette. " And Other Brilliant Insights.
and links.

Not only are their policies made in DEAland, so are their clichés.

Earlier this year, Toronto police Chief Julian Fantino said THC levels in Canadian cannabis have become so high that marijuana could no longer be considered a " soft drug, " comparing it to cocaine or heroin. That is straight out of the DEA handbook.
See
New Toronto Police Endorses Death Penalty For Marijuana Dealers. Lies About Dutch.

Nonetheless, in Canada the politicization of law enforcement is less pervasive than in DEAland, because almost no law enforcement personnel are elected. This means that the Canadian police lack the powerful political support they have in DEAland from elected DAs and sheriffs.

There is also a great deal of establishment skepticism about cannabis prohibition in Canada. Nonetheless, the Canadian people and media are going to have to wake up to the very pernicious role the Canadian narks are playing in their public discourse under the tutelage of the DEA.
See
The Police From Two Countries Meet To Conspire Against The Liberties Of Their Citizens.

Also the Canadian people are going to have to recognize the damage done to the public discourse by the tabloids owned by the Canoe group of Quebecor Media, -- The Sun papers in most Canadian cities, except for Vancouver. Their editorial pages are insulting to the intelligence of anyone who is as semi-literate as their editors.
See
Article From The Calgary Sun Is So Dumb That Reading It Could Cause Brain Damage. Prohibitionist Drivel At Its Worst.

The excellent Canadian Senate report also puts the burden on the prohibitionist to prove that their policies work, instead of just debating the purported dangers of cannabis. The inestimable Dan Gardner of the Ottawa Citizen said that the most important thing about the report was that it eliminated the snicker factor with which prohibitionists have always dismissed any discussion of cannabis.
See
Conservative Canadian Senator Calls For Commission To Review All Drug Laws:
" Should marijuana be legalized? " Article and Text Of Resolution
and
Scathing Column In Ottawa Citizen Attacks Health Minister's Rationing Of Medical Marijuana... And Justice.
and
Canadian Justice Minister's Bizarre Non-Response to Ottawa Citizen's Dan Gardner.

They cannot simply dismiss the report as a back to school gift to drug pushers and get away with it anymore, but the response of the prohibitionists has been predictable and very weak.

The leader of the Canadian Alliance, the small conservative party that has a few Parliamentary seats in the western provinces immediately announced that he thought that cannabis is more dangerous than alcohol.
See
Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.

Even the Vancouver police chief reaffirmed his faith in the doctrine of the blessed Gateway Theory.

However, Senator Nolin, who headed the committee, is one of the few public officials who really understands what is going on. He is more than capable of defending himself in a debate, and he is not going to be quiet about the issue just because he has finished the report.

Consequently, a national debate on cannabis prohibition in Canada is a very real prospect. One of the issues that will dominate the debate is the role of the DEAland in shaping Canadian laws.

Witness The Washington Post story on the Canadian Senate report in which they quoted the Canadian Police Association's David Griffin as saying that Canada surpassed Mexico as a supplier of marijuana to the United States.

That is absurd. Seizures at the Canadian border are only one percent of those at the Mexican border.
See
How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works on the Texas/Mexico Border. Contrast with the Situation at the Canadian Border. Great Journalism.
and
Edmonton Police Actually Claim That Canadian Marijuana Is Being Exported To Mexico If You Believe That

But it is the one point that will be used by DEAland prohibitionists to justify supporting Canadian narks in their campaign against Canadian sovereignty.

It is hardly a coincidence that Griffin told this particular lie to the Post. The Post says, He cited an international narcotics control board report that found that Canada produces 800 tons of the drug annually, of which more than 60 percent enters the illegal market in the United States.

That is contradicted by the RCMP's own web site.
See
RCMP Report On Marijuana Trafficking Contradicts The Party Line
About Marijuana Smuggling From Canada To DEAland. Far More Goes North Than South
and
http://www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/html/drugsituation.htm#Marihuana
and
Ottawa Citizen Columnist Dan Gardner Assails Canadian Justice Minister's Kowtowing to UN and DEAland Narks: " U.S. says jump, we say how high? "

Nonetheless, The Post quotes him as saying, " The more liberalized our drug laws, the more that industry will grow in producing drugs for the United States. "

I think that this proves that the Canadian police are not only a danger to the personal freedom of Canadian citizens, but also a threat to Canadian sovereignty.

That must be part of the national debate in Canada, but also in the UK and ultimately even in DEAland. Prohibitionism is a supranational ideology that is the basis of a global grab for power.
